pages.title: Red Giant Envelope
pages.text: When a star exhausts the hydrogen in its core it swells, and its outer layers expand and cool to a dull red. The Sun will do this in about five billion years. The envelope is enormous and tenuous, a thin, glowing fog that barely seems to weigh anything.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Running a stellar core in the Nucleosynthesis Chamber past hydrogen exhaustion, I watched its outer layers puff outward. Separating the swollen envelope from the core left me with this bloated fog.
